mainEntity.name: Can structural steel framing be added to an existing wood or masonry building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, structural steel can be integrated into existing wood, masonry, or concrete buildings, usually to remove load-bearing walls or support building additions. When opening up a floor plan, contractors often insert a steel I-beam supported by steel posts to carry the upper-floor or roof weight previously held by multiple studs. A structural engineer must review the existing structure to confirm the loads can transfer down to the foundation, which may require pouring new concrete footings beneath the new steel posts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, steel beams and columns can replace load-bearing walls in existing structures, provided an engineer confirms that the foundation can support the concentrated loads.
